## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge this yet. The new `Cache.set` stores keys as given, but `get` lower-cases them, so any value set under a key that isn't all lowercase can't be read back. The round-trip test only uses lowercase keys, so it doesn't catch this.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — `set` writes `self._store[key]` without lower-casing the key, but `get` (app/cache.py:17) looks up `key.lower()`. So `c.set("Alpha", 1); c.get("Alpha")` returns `None`, and the entry under `"Alpha"` is never removed by `get`'s expiry branch either. This also breaks the rule in the comment at app/cache.py:14-15 ("every path into _store lower-cases the key first"). Could `set` write to `self._store[key.lower()]`? A mixed-case key in `test_set_then_get_round_trip` (e.g. `c.set("Alpha", 1)`) would then catch this, since the test's lowercase `"alpha"` passes either way — impact: callers moving off direct `_store` writes, as the PR intends, get silent cache misses for any key with an uppercase letter. Those dead entries also pile up in `_store` because nothing ever evicts them.

## Strengths
- `test_entries_expire` patches `time.monotonic` on the `time` module, which is the same name `app/cache.py` calls. That makes the expiry check deterministic and makes it actually test `set`'s expiry calculation and `get`'s eviction.
- The updated comment at app/cache.py:7 ("Entries expire 300 seconds after they are written.") matches `DEFAULT_TTL = 300`. The default argument in `__init__` picks up the new value.
